title: How to organise the dry goods shelves | Pantry
description:
Holds the grains, pasta and cereals you actually cook from in a normal week.

This is the Dry Goods Shelves in the Pantry. About 45-75 min.

WHAT DONE LOOKS LIKE
Every opened bag is either sealed in a container with its opening date written on it, or gone. Pasta, rice and oats stand as one block, breakfast cereal as another, and you can read the level in every container from the doorway without lifting a thing.

THE SIX PASSES
Sort: Bring down every bag and box, open the ones already opened, and smell the flour and the oats.
Straighten: Rice, pasta and oats go at chest height, in the arc your arm makes when you are already holding a pan.

Safety: Fall, cut, or crush: cereal boxes and heavy grain containers stacked above shoulder height come down on somebo
Standardize: One container style for staples, one label per container carrying the item and the date you opened it, so a lo
Sustain: When you put the shopping away, the new bag of rice goes behind the open one and never in front of it.

THE STANDARD YOU LEAVE BEHIND
Staples live in one container style, labeled with the item and the date it was opened, filled front to back with the oldest bag at the front.
